quests.instruction: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving car?
quests.hint: Think about every seat in the car, front and back.
quests.explanation: Everyone in a car, in the front and the back, must wear a seat belt. In a crash, an unbelted person can be thrown around the car, even at slow speeds.
quests.funFact: Seat belts are one of the most effective safety inventions for cars.

quests.instruction: What should you do first when you get into a car, before it starts moving?
quests.hint: Listen for the click.
quests.explanation: Fastening your seat belt before the car moves keeps you safe if it has to stop suddenly. It only takes a second.
quests.funFact: Many cars beep until everyone has buckled up.

quests.instruction: Which passenger may need a booster seat so the seat belt fits properly?
quests.hint: This passenger is bigger than a baby but not yet tall enough for the belt to fit.
quests.explanation: A booster seat lifts a child so the belt lies across the strong parts of the body. It is used until the child is tall enough for the belt alone.
quests.funFact: Rules about child seats depend on a child's height, weight, or age, and differ between countries.

quests.instruction: Which should you do before you cross a road?
quests.hint: Use this before your feet.
quests.explanation: Looking carefully both ways lets you see vehicles you might not hear. Cross only when the road is clear.
quests.funFact: Drivers may not see walkers who step out suddenly, so looking first matters.

quests.instruction: At a crossing, which colour of the walking-person signal means 'wait on the pavement'?
quests.hint: It is the same colour as a stop sign.
quests.explanation: A red person means wait. Wait for the green person, then check again that traffic has stopped before you cross.
quests.funFact: Some crossings have a button you press to ask for the green person.

quests.instruction: Which should you put away while you cross the road?
quests.hint: It takes your eyes and attention away from traffic.
quests.explanation: Looking at a phone makes it easy to miss traffic. Keep your eyes and ears on the road until you reach the other side.
quests.funFact: Some cities have put lights into the pavement so people looking down can still see the crossing signal.

quests.instruction: A ball rolls into the road. What should you do?
quests.hint: A ball can be replaced, but you cannot.
quests.explanation: Never run after a ball into the road. A driver may not see you in time to stop. Ask an adult for help or wait until the road is clear.
quests.funFact: Drivers need time to react and then stop, especially on faster roads.

quests.instruction: A stranger in a car offers you a ride home. What should you do?
quests.hint: Do not go with someone you do not know.
quests.explanation: Never accept a ride from someone you do not know, even if they seem friendly. Say no, move away, and tell a trusted adult.
quests.funFact: Many families agree on a safe word that only trusted people know.

quests.instruction: Is it safe to walk, play, or take shortcuts along railway tracks?
quests.hint: Trains move fast and cannot swerve.
quests.explanation: Railway tracks are dangerous because trains move fast and cannot stop quickly or swerve. Only cross at official crossings.
quests.funFact: A train can take hundreds of metres to stop after the driver applies the brakes.

quests.instruction: When is the best time for a beginner to practise cycling outdoors?
quests.hint: Drivers can see you best at this time.
quests.explanation: In daylight, drivers and walkers can see you more easily, and you can see the ground. Beginners should avoid riding in darkness, fog, or heavy rain.
quests.funFact: Even in daylight, bright clothes and lights help others notice cyclists.

quests.instruction: Which is the safest place for a beginner to practise riding a bicycle?
quests.hint: There are no cars here, only space to wobble.
quests.explanation: A quiet park or traffic-free path lets beginners practise balancing and braking without worrying about vehicles.
quests.funFact: Many towns have practice areas where children can learn cycling skills.

quests.instruction: Headphones can make cycling more dangerous because they block which sense?
quests.hint: You need it to hear horns and engines.
quests.explanation: Cyclists need to hear approaching traffic, bells, and horns. Loud headphones can hide these sounds.
quests.funFact: In some places, wearing headphones while riding is discouraged or against the rules.

quests.instruction: On a plane, which card in the seat pocket shows the exits and what to do in an emergency?
quests.hint: It uses pictures to explain what to do.
quests.explanation: Every airline provides a safety card for each type of aircraft. Reading it helps you know where the nearest exit is.
quests.funFact: Safety cards use pictures so people who speak any language can understand.

quests.instruction: The seat belt sign comes on because of bumpy air. What should passengers do?
quests.hint: Stay put.
quests.explanation: Bumpy air, called turbulence, can toss people who are standing. Staying seated with your belt fastened keeps you safe.
quests.funFact: Pilots can often warn passengers about bumpy air ahead.

quests.instruction: Which is a safe place for children to play?
quests.hint: It is built for fun, not for vehicles.
quests.explanation: Playgrounds are designed for play. Roads and railways are for vehicles, and they can be very dangerous.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds are fenced to keep children away from nearby roads.

quests.instruction: At dusk, which jacket colour is easiest for drivers to notice?
quests.hint: Choose the colour that glows against the evening light.
quests.explanation: Bright colours such as orange or yellow stand out. Dark colours blend into the dusk, so add reflective strips too.
quests.funFact: Bright colours help in daylight, while reflective strips work best in the dark.

quests.instruction: A lorry driver can only see you if you can see which part of the lorry?
quests.hint: It is a shiny surface the driver uses to look behind and beside the lorry.
quests.explanation: If you cannot see a lorry driver's mirror, the driver cannot see you. Keep away from the sides and back of big vehicles.
quests.funFact: Big trucks have blind spots right behind and beside them.

quests.instruction: Which parked vehicle could hide a small child from an approaching driver?
quests.hint: Think big and tall.
quests.explanation: Tall vehicles block the view. Never step out from behind a parked van or bus. Walk to a place where you can see and be seen.
quests.funFact: Drivers are taught to slow down near parked vehicles because people may step out.

quests.instruction: Which loose item must be kept away from escalators and train doors so it does not get caught?
quests.hint: It is long, soft, and worn around the neck.
quests.explanation: Long scarves, shoelaces, and bag straps can get caught in moving parts. Tuck them in, and hold the handrail on an escalator.
quests.funFact: Many escalators have signs reminding passengers to keep loose clothing and shoelaces tied.

quests.instruction: To avoid slipping into the gap between a train and the platform, what should you watch as you step across?
quests.hint: It moves across the gap, one careful step at a time.
quests.explanation: The gap can be wide or uneven. Look down and take a careful step, especially with luggage or a pram.
quests.funFact: Many stations announce 'mind the gap' because the train and platform do not always line up.

quests.instruction: On a ferry deck, who should young children stay close to?
quests.hint: Someone who looks after you.
quests.explanation: Decks can be slippery and have gaps near the edge. Young children should stay close to a trusted adult.
quests.funFact: Ferries have railings and signs to keep people away from the edge.

quests.instruction: Which red cylinder is kept on boats and buses to put out small fires?
quests.hint: It holds something that smothers flames.
quests.explanation: A fire extinguisher sprays something that smothers the flames. Only trained adults should use it, and everyone else should get out and call for help.
quests.funFact: Buses, ships, and trains are usually required to carry fire extinguishers.

quests.instruction: Which item from a first-aid kit covers a small cut or scrape?
quests.hint: It is sticky on one side.
quests.explanation: A bandage keeps a small wound clean. For anything serious, tell an adult and get help.
quests.funFact: Many ferries, long-distance buses, and trains carry first-aid kits.

quests.instruction: Which symbol is used around the world to ask for urgent help?
quests.hint: Ships, aircraft, and mountain rescuers all understand it.
quests.explanation: SOS is an international call for help. It has been used by ships, aircraft, and mountain rescue.
quests.funFact: In Morse code, SOS is three short signals, three long signals, then three short signals.

quests.instruction: Thick fog covers the road. What should drivers do with their speed?
quests.hint: They need extra time to react.
quests.explanation: Fog hides the road ahead, so drivers slow down and keep a big gap. This gives them time to react.
quests.funFact: Fog lights help drivers see and be seen in thick fog.

quests.instruction: A thunderstorm starts while you are waiting for a bus outdoors. Where is the safest place to wait?
quests.hint: Choose a solid shelter, not an open space or a tree.
quests.explanation: Lightning can strike trees and open ground. Go indoors or into a solid shelter and wait until the storm passes.
quests.funFact: Cars with metal roofs can also protect people from lightning.

quests.instruction: The pavement is icy. Which footwear gives the best grip?
quests.hint: Look for deep, rubbery soles.
quests.explanation: Boots with deep soles grip slippery ground better than sandals or smooth shoes. Walk slowly with small steps.
quests.funFact: Some boots have spikes or studs for icy paths.

quests.instruction: A bicycle built for one person can safely carry how many riders?
quests.hint: Count the saddles.
quests.explanation: Bicycles are made for one rider. Carrying two makes it hard to balance and steer, and can cause falls.
quests.funFact: Special bicycles with two seats, called tandems, are made for two riders.

quests.instruction: Which fallen item can make railway tracks slippery in autumn and make it harder for trains to stop?
quests.hint: Trees drop them at that time of year.
quests.explanation: Wet leaves on rails can be as slippery as ice. Trains may brake earlier and run slower on affected lines.
quests.funFact: Some railways use special trains to clean leaves from the tracks.

quests.instruction: When a fast train passes a platform without stopping, what rushes along beside it?
quests.hint: You can feel it, but you cannot see it.
quests.explanation: A fast train pushes air along with it, creating a strong rush of wind. This is one reason to stay well behind the line.
quests.funFact: Station announcements warn passengers to stand back when fast trains pass.
